scope_notes: Covers instep drive (shooting/long ball), inside-foot pass, receiving/first touch, dribbling & 1v1 feints, heading (with US Soccer age limits), and cutting/landing mechanics from FIFA 11+. Goalkeeping is NOT covered (gap).
source_gap_notes: Kicking biomechanics are well researched; passing/receiving cues come mostly from US Soccer and FIFA coaching resources (several reviewed only via abstracts/snippets). Dribbling relies on Coerver Coaching.

sources.credibility: Official US Soccer coaching curriculum (hosted by a state association).

sources.credibility: US Soccer licensing course content (higher level).

sources.credibility: FIFA's official coaching platform, elite session on directional first touch.

sources.name: FIFA 11+ injury prevention programme manual
sources.credibility: FIFA Medical (F-MARC) warm-up programme with balance, single-leg strength, plyometric landing and cutting exercises; extensive RCT evidence.

sources.credibility: Randomized trial showing FIFA 11+ changes landing kinematics (dynamic knee valgus).

sources.credibility: US Soccer Learning Center resource pack for the Concussion Initiative (brain-health guidance for coaches, referees, parents, players). Age-specific heading rules are taken from SO13.

sources.credibility: Key review of kicking mechanics: approach, support leg, proximal-to-distal sequence, foot-ball impact.

sources.credibility: Review of instep kick kinematics/kinetics and determinants of ball speed.

sources.credibility: Review emphasizing whole-body (trunk/arm) contribution to the maximal instep kick.

sources.credibility: US Youth Soccer national policy: no heading for age 10 and under; ages 11-12 may head in matches, practice capped at 25 headers per player per week; 13+ unrestricted.

sources.name: Coerver Coaching - Tips to improve 1v1 soccer skills: Feints

skills.name: Instep drive (shooting / driven ball)
skills.recommended_camera: Side view from the kicking-leg side at ball height and a front/rear view along the ball's line; 120-240 fps.

checkpoints.description: Angled approach (roughly 30-45 deg) to the ball allows pelvis rotation and a longer swing.
checkpoints.measurable_angle_or_rule: approach path angle ~30-45 deg to the intended ball direction

checkpoints.description: Support foot planted beside and slightly behind the ball, roughly 1-1.5 ft to the side, toes pointing at the target.
checkpoints.measurable_angle_or_rule: support foot ~30-45 cm (about 1-1.5 ft) to the side of the ball and slightly behind it; support toe direction within ~15 deg of target line

checkpoints.description: Support knee flexes on landing to absorb load, then extends during the swing.
checkpoints.measurable_angle_or_rule: support knee flexion at plant ~20-40 deg, decreasing toward impact

checkpoints.description: Proximal-to-distal sequence: pelvis rotates and the thigh drives forward, then the thigh decelerates as the shank whips through (knee extension) to impact.
checkpoints.measurable_angle_or_rule: thigh angular velocity peaks before shank angular velocity; maximal knee flexion (~90-110 deg) at end of backswing

checkpoints.description: Contact with the instep (laces) with the ankle locked in plantar flexion; body over the ball for a low drive.
checkpoints.measurable_angle_or_rule: ankle plantar-flexed (foot pointing down) at impact; shoulder midpoint over or ahead of the ball for low shots

checkpoints.description: Opposite arm swings out/back for balance and trunk contribution.
checkpoints.measurable_angle_or_rule: non-kicking-side arm abducted away from the body during the swing

faults.name: Planting too far from / behind the ball
faults.video_signs: Support foot lands far behind or wide of the ball; player reaches for the ball.
faults.correction_cue: 'Plant next to the ball, toe to the target.'
faults.why_it_matters: Poor plant position changes foot-ball contact and reduces control and ball speed.

faults.name: Leaning back
faults.video_signs: Trunk leans backward at impact; ball balloons over the goal.
faults.correction_cue: 'Chest over the ball, land on your kicking foot.'
faults.why_it_matters: Backward lean shifts contact below the ball's centre.

faults.name: Toe-poke / floppy ankle
faults.video_signs: Contact with the toes or ankle not locked; inconsistent ball flight.
faults.correction_cue: 'Point the toe down, lock the ankle, strike with the laces.'
faults.why_it_matters: A locked instep gives a firmer, more efficient impact.

faults.name: Straight-on approach / no hip rotation
faults.video_signs: Approach directly behind the ball; small backswing; kick from the knee only.
faults.correction_cue: 'Come in on an angle and swing from the hip.'
faults.why_it_matters: An angled approach permits pelvis rotation and a longer, faster swing.

drills.name: Plant-foot gate drill
drills.setup: Place two cones forming a small 'gate' beside the ball where the support foot should land.
steps: Approach from an angle and plant the support foot inside the gate, toes to target.
Strike at ~50% power, freeze on landing.
Increase power as the plant becomes consistent; film from the front.
drills.why: A physical target for the support foot makes the most influential set-up variable concrete and repeatable.

drills.name: Wall driven-ball progression
drills.setup: Ball 5-10 m from a wall or rebounder.
steps: Strike stationary balls with the laces, ankle locked, chest over the ball.
Aim for a low target (tape line ~1 m high).
Progress to a ball rolled in from the side, then a one-touch strike.
drills.fixes: Toe-poke; leaning back; no hip rotation
drills.why: Short distances give many repetitions and a clear low target highlights whether the body is over the ball.

pro_tips.tip: The maximal kick is a whole-body skill: trunk rotation and arm action contribute to the leg's speed, not just the kicking leg.
The support leg absorbs landing load with knee flexion and then extends to help accelerate the swing - strong single-leg strength helps kicking.

skills.name: Inside-of-foot pass
skills.recommended_camera: Front view along the passing line and a side view.

checkpoints.description: Support foot beside the ball pointing at the target; passing foot turned out (~90 deg) with the ankle locked.
checkpoints.measurable_angle_or_rule: passing foot rotated ~70-90 deg outward relative to the target line at contact

checkpoints.description: Contact through the middle of the ball for a firm, ground pass; follow through toward the target.
checkpoints.measurable_angle_or_rule: kicking ankle travels along the target line after contact

checkpoints.description: Head up / scanning before the pass.
checkpoints.measurable_angle_or_rule: head orientation rises above the ball (looks up) at least once in the 2 s before the pass

faults.name: Toe-down / floppy ankle on pass
faults.video_signs: Passing foot not locked; ball bobbles or veers.
faults.correction_cue: 'Lock the ankle, toe up, heel down.'
faults.why_it_matters: A firm surface gives an accurate, predictable pass.

faults.name: Soft, bouncing passes
faults.video_signs: Ball lifts or rolls slowly; contact under the ball.
faults.correction_cue: 'Strike through the middle - firm and on the ground.'
faults.why_it_matters: US Soccer guidance stresses firm, accurate ground passes.

drills.name: Passing gates
drills.setup: Pairs with cone gates (1-2 m wide) spaced around a grid.
steps: Pass through a gate to a partner, then move to a new gate.
Receiver receives across the body and passes back through another gate.
Progress to two-touch then one-touch.
drills.fixes: Floppy ankle; soft passes; no scanning
drills.why: Gates demand accuracy and force players to look up to find the next gate, linking technique to scanning.

pro_tips.tip: Coach passing and receiving as one continuous action, then move quickly into small-sided pressured games where decisions are made.

skills.name: Receiving / first touch
skills.recommended_camera: Side view and an elevated view if possible to see body orientation.

checkpoints.description: Open body orientation (half-turned) before the ball arrives, so the receiver can see the field and play forward.
checkpoints.measurable_angle_or_rule: hip line angled ~30-60 deg to the incoming pass line (not square to it)

checkpoints.description: Directional first touch away from pressure and into space, without stopping the ball dead.
checkpoints.measurable_angle_or_rule: ball travels > ~1 m in the intended direction after the first touch
one or more head turns away from the ball in the seconds before reception

faults.name: Square/closed body shape
faults.video_signs: Receiver faces the passer squarely and must take extra touches to turn.
faults.correction_cue: 'Open up - receive on the back foot.'
faults.why_it_matters: An open stance lets the first touch go forward.

faults.name: Stopping the ball dead
faults.video_signs: First touch kills the ball under the feet; second touch needed to move.
faults.correction_cue: 'Take it with you - touch into space.'
faults.why_it_matters: A directional touch saves time and beats pressure.

drills.name: Directional first-touch gates
drills.setup: Receiver in a central zone with cone gates on each side; a passive defender points to one side.
steps: Server passes in.
Receiver scans to see where the defender is.
First touch through the gate away from pressure.
Progress to an active defender.
drills.fixes: Closed body shape; ball stopped dead; no scanning
drills.why: The defender's cue makes scanning necessary and rewards touching away from pressure, mirroring match demands.

pro_tips.tip: FIFA's elite sessions treat the first touch as a decision: direct it toward the next action, not just under control.

skills.name: Dribbling and 1v1 feints
skills.recommended_camera: Front view (from the defender's perspective) and side view.

checkpoints.description: The touch before the feint sets it up: if the ball is too close or too far from the body, the feint is hard to execute.
checkpoints.measurable_angle_or_rule: ball roughly 0.5-1 m ahead of the feet at the moment of the feint

checkpoints.description: Body feint: drop the shoulder and shift weight onto one leg to sell the fake.
checkpoints.measurable_angle_or_rule: clear lateral shoulder dip/hip shift (> ~10 cm) toward the fake direction

checkpoints.description: Explosive acceleration out of the move - once the defender is beaten, explode away.
checkpoints.measurable_angle_or_rule: step frequency/velocity increases immediately after the feint

faults.name: Poor set-up touch (too close or too far)
faults.video_signs: Ball is jammed under the feet or runs too far ahead right before the move.
faults.correction_cue: 'Set the ball - one good touch, then the move.'

faults.name: Weak feint / no acceleration
faults.video_signs: Fake is small and the player doesn't speed up afterward.
faults.why_it_matters: A feint only works if the attacker accelerates while the defender is off balance.

drills.name: 1v1 feint progression (Coerver style)
steps: Repeat the move against a cone without pressure.
Then against a passive helper defender.
Then live 1v1 with full tackling to an end line.
drills.fixes: Ball too far ahead; weak feint
drills.why: Progressing from no pressure to full pressure builds a reliable move before it is tested live.

pro_tips.tip: Coerver breaks 1v1 play into three parts - changes of direction, feints, and stops-and-starts - and stresses that acceleration after the move is what actually beats the defender.

checkpoints.description: Contact the ball with the forehead (hairline), eyes open, neck braced, power from the trunk.
checkpoints.measurable_angle_or_rule: trunk extends then flexes forward into contact; head and trunk move together

faults.name: Heading with the top of the head / eyes closed
faults.video_signs: Ball contacts the crown; head flinches.
faults.why_it_matters: Correct contact improves control and comfort.

pro_tips.tip: Youth heading rules (US Youth Soccer Rule 305, aligned with the US Soccer Concussion Initiative): age 10 and under - no heading in matches or organized practice; ages 11-12 - may head in matches, practice heading capped at 25 headers per player per week; 13+ - no age restriction. Check your league's current rules.

skills.name: Cutting and landing mechanics (FIFA 11+)
skills.recommended_camera: Front view (to see knee alignment) at 60+ fps.

checkpoints.description: Knee stays over the toes (no inward collapse / dynamic knee valgus) when landing, squatting on one leg or planting to cut.
checkpoints.measurable_angle_or_rule: frontal-plane projection angle of the knee < ~10-15 deg of valgus; knee stays between hip and 2nd toe line

checkpoints.description: Soft landings on the balls of the feet with hip and knee flexion.
checkpoints.measurable_angle_or_rule: knee flexion increases to > ~45-60 deg during landing absorption

faults.name: Knee valgus collapse
faults.video_signs: Knee moves inward toward the midline on landing or plant.
faults.why_it_matters: Dynamic knee valgus is a recognized ACL injury mechanism and is reduced by the FIFA 11+ program.

drills.name: FIFA 11+ part 2 strength/plyometric/balance block
drills.setup: Field area; partner for some exercises.
steps: Single-leg stance with ball exchanges.
Single-leg squats with knee over toe.
Vertical, lateral and box jumps with soft landings.
Plant-and-cut running with controlled knee alignment.
drills.dosage: Full FIFA 11+ warm-up ~20 min, at least 2x per week
drills.why: Repeated, cued practice of knee alignment under progressively harder balance and jump tasks builds neuromuscular control; trials show reduced dynamic knee valgus after 8-10 weeks.

pro_tips.tip: Use FIFA 11+ (or 11+ Kids for younger players) as the standard warm-up at least twice per week.
